newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives lose ground in Scotland - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives lose ground in Scotland - poll.

text.p: The popularity of Britain's ruling Conservative Party has fallen again in Scotland while Labour and the Scottish nationalists have made gains, an opinion poll showed on Monday.
A System Three poll for the Herald newspaper shows the Conservatives in third place with 15 percent, one point down on last month.
Labour are up two points to 52 percent, while the Scottish National Party remains in second place at 25 percent -- three points up on the last poll.
The Liberal Democrats are still in fourth place at eight percent, a drop of two points.
System Three polled 1,048 people in 40 constituencies between January 23 and 28.
Prime Minister John Major, whose Conservative Party is trailing Labour by around 20 points in nationwide opinion polls, must call a general election by May.
